correctness.rationale: Formal arch/remainder decomposition yields A_q and R_{q,j} by independent first-appearance order counting. Barker et al. Proposition 15 supplies the explicit palindrome-index reduction, credited as prior. The even and odd center counts produce one rational bivariate formula. Minimal length follows from exact arch size and a forced complementary center. A renewal process with independent coupon-collector completion times has mean qH_q and variance q^2 H_q^(2)-qH_q, giving the displayed central limit theorem with variance factor 2. The shipped verifier calculates actual subsequence universality rather than relying on the lemma and checks full distributions q=2..5 in exhaustive finite windows. Proof extends to all q and n without assuming those checks are exhaustive.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal formula for unrestricted q-ary words is not a stronger formula for symmetric palindromes, since the pairs of mirrored positions are not independent. There remains a risk a separate general result can specialize to this formula.

value.rationale: Palindromes are a canonical nonregular class whose mirrored letters create globally correlated subsequence statistics. For all alphabet sizes, the finding resolves the complete natural length-index counting distribution, not a tiny arbitrary slice; identifies every shortest-length extremal multiplicity; and gives the typical index fluctuations through a Gaussian law. These results supply concrete benchmark distributions for symmetry-constrained subsequence coverage. This extends the value beyond the previously established index test for a single palindrome, without asserting a new structural symmetry lemma or a paper-sized advance.
